# package.xml reference

This page is for developers who write or change a `package.xml` by hand. It lists every element and attribute that
`eZPackage` understands, how it reads each one (`eZPackage::parseDOMTree()`), how it writes it back
(`eZPackage::domStructure()`), and the traps between the two. All references are to
`kernel/classes/ezpackage.php` unless another file is named.

## How the file is read

- The reader looks most elements up with `getElementsByTagName()`, which finds an element **anywhere** below the
  root and takes the first one. Keep every element where the writer puts it; do not reuse an element name inside
  another element (the one exception the reader handles is `<version>`, read with XPath as a direct child of
  `<package>`, so `<ezpublish><version>` does not get in its way).
- A definition **without a root element or without a non-empty `<name>`** is not a package: it is not read, and
  the package lists skip it.
- `<version><number>`, `<version><release>` and `<type value>` must each be absent, empty, or a plain token of 1 to
  64 characters from `0-9 A-Z a-z . _ + -` (`isValidDefinitionToken()`). Anything else and the whole definition is
  refused.
- A JSON package (`package.json`) is turned into the same DOM first, so everything below applies to both formats.

## The root element

```xml
<package version="3.5.2" development="false" install_type="install">
```

| Attribute | Read | Written |
|---|---|---|
| `install_type` | `install` (default) or `import`; see [Import versus install](import-versus-install.md) | always |
| `development` | `"true"` means development, anything else not | always, `false` |
| `version` | not read | always `eZPackage::VERSION`, `3.5.2` (the format version, not the package version) |
| other attributes (the 7x site packages carry `is_active="true"`) | not read | not written |

## Description elements

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | **yes** | The package name. On import it must pass `eZPackage::isValidName()` (letters of either case, digits, `_` and `-`, not starting with `-`), else `STATUS_INVALID_NAME`. It is also the directory name in the repository |
| `<summary>` | no | One line; the setup wizard shows it as the site's title and `[site_details] Title` defaults to it |
| `<description>` | no | Longer text |
| `<vendor>` | no | Chooses the repository directory: the vendor run through the `urlalias` transformation (`7x` stays `7x`, `eZ systems` becomes `ez-systems`); without a vendor the package goes to `local` |
| `<type value="..."/>` | no | The package type, trimmed; see [Package types](package-types.md) |
| `<priority value="..."/>` | no | Kept and filterable in `eZPackage::fetchPackages()`; nothing in the installer uses it |
| `<extension name="..."/>` | no | The extension a package belongs to; filterable in `fetchPackages()` |
| `<source>` | no | Free text |
| `<ezpublish><version>`, `<named-version>` | no | The Exponential version the package was made with (`6.0.15-stable`, `6.0` in sevenx_multisite). Kept for information: the package code does not compare it with the running version. The element name is historical and stays as it is |

## People, packaging and history

```xml
<maintainers>
  <maintainer><name>...</name><email>...</email><role>lead</role></maintainer>
</maintainers>
<packaging><timestamp>1705211779</timestamp><host>...</host><packager>...</packager></packaging>
<documents><document mime-type="text/plain" name="LICENCE" os="" audience=""/></documents>
<groups><group name="..."/></groups>
<changelog>
  <entry timestamp="..." person="..." email="..." release="1"><change>Creation of package.</change></entry>
</changelog>
```

| Element | Notes |
|---|---|
| `<maintainer>` | `name`, `email`, optional `role`; the roles offered are `[MaintainerSettings] RoleList[]`: `lead`, `developer`, `designer`, `contributor`, `tester` |
| `<packaging>` | When and where the archive was made. Without it the package reads as "not packaged" (no time, no host) |
| `<document>` | A file in `documents/`; `name` and `mime-type`, optional `os` and `audience` |
| `<group>` | Free group names |
| `<entry>` | One per release, attributes `timestamp`, `person`, `email`, `release`, one `<change>` per change |

What a published package must fill in is in [Documentation requirements](../requirements/README.md).

## Release elements

```xml
<version><number>6.0</number><release>15-stable</release></version>
<timestamp>1705211779</timestamp>
<licence>GPL</licence>
<state>stable</state>
```

| Element | Notes |
|---|---|
| `<version><number>` | The version number, trimmed. New packages from the wizards get a strict SemVer 2.0.0 number; reading stays tolerant (`kernel/classes/ezpackageversion.php`) |
| `<version><release>` | The release number, trimmed. `eZPackage::getVersion()` joins them as `<number>-<release>`; that string is what `min-version` is compared with and what the `ezpackage` table records |
| `<timestamp>` | The release time; only a `<timestamp>` that is a direct child of `<package>` counts |
| `<licence>` | The license identifier; matched against `package.ini [LicenseSettings]` (`AliasList[GPL]=GPL-2.0-or-later` makes `GPL` known). An unknown value is shown as it is. The element keeps its historical spelling |
| `<state>` | One of `[PackageSettings] StateList[]`: `mature`, `stable`, `beta`, `alpha`, `prealpha` |

## Files

```xml
<simple-files>
  <simple-file key="..." original-path="..." package-path="simplefiles/24ec46f7.jpg"/>
</simple-files>
<files>
  <collection name="default">
    <file-list type="thumbnail" variable-name="thumbnail">
      <file name="thumbnail.png" md5sum="77a7bc0cc6e1e5138ca7a6e39a130307"/>
    </file-list>
  </collection>
</files>
```

| Element | Attributes |
|---|---|
| `<simple-file>` | `key`, `original-path`, `package-path` (below `simplefiles/`) |
| `<collection>` | `name`; a `<files>` without `<collection>` is read as one collection named by its own `name` |
| `<file-list>` | `type` (`file`, `design`, `ini`, `thumbnail`, `image` ...), `design`, `role`, `role-value`, `variable-name` |
| `<file>` | `name`, `sub-directory`, `path` (where it came from), `md5sum`, `type` (`dir` for a directory), `variable-name` |

The first `thumbnail` file of the `default` collection is the picture the setup wizard shows for a site package
(`thumbnail-list`).

## Dependencies

```xml
<dependencies>
  <provides/>
  <requires>
    <require type="ezpackage" name="sevenx_classes" min-version="5.1"/>
  </requires>
  <obsoletes/>
  <conflicts/>
</dependencies>
```

Four sections with the items `<provide>`, `<require>`, `<obsolete>` and `<conflict>`. The reader keeps every
attribute of an item. The installer acts on `<require type="ezpackage">` with `name` and `min-version`; see
[Dependencies and install order](dependencies-and-install-order.md). A design package of 7x declares
`<provide type="ezfile" name="collection" value="default"/>`.

## Install scripts: settings

```xml
<settings>
  <settings-file filename="install-scripts.php"/>
</settings>
```

Each `filename` is a PHP file in the package's `settings/` directory that the Create sites step includes. See
[Install scripts in a site package](install-scripts-in-a-site-package.md).

## Install and uninstall items

```xml
<install>
  <item type="ezcontentclass" filename="class-article" sub-directory="ezcontentclass"/>
  <item type="ezfile" collection="default"/>
</install>
<uninstall>
  <item type="ezcontentclass" filename="class-article" sub-directory="ezcontentclass"/>
</uninstall>
```

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | The handler, looked up in `[PackageSettings] HandlerAlias[]` |
| `filename`, `sub-directory` | The item's document: `<sub-directory>/<filename>.xml` (or `.json`) |
| `name`, `os` | Optional; `os` narrows an item to one operating system in `installItemsList()` |
| handler attributes | Read by the handler: `collection` (`ezfile`), `original-path` and `database-type` (`ezsql`) |

What each type does is in [Install items and handlers](install-items-and-handlers.md).

## Metadata and install data

- `<metadata><entry key="expai.provenance">value</entry></metadata>`: free strings kept with a package by tools,
  written only when there is any (`eZPackage::setMetadata()`).
- `<install-data><data type="..."><element name="" value=""/><array name="">...</array></data></install-data>`:
  what handlers remember between install and uninstall; written by the kernel, not by hand.

## What is lost when the kernel writes a package

`domStructure()` writes the elements in a fixed order (name, summary, description, vendor, priority, type,
extension, source, ezpublish, maintainers, packaging, documents, groups, changelog, simple-files, files, version,
timestamp, licence, state, dependencies, install, uninstall, install-data, metadata). Keep these differences in
mind before you let the kernel rewrite a hand-made file:

> **Note**
> Fixed in 6.0.15: `domStructure()` writes `<settings>` (after `<dependencies>`) and every attribute of a
> dependency item. Before, a site package stored again by the kernel lost its install scripts' list and the
> `min-version` of its `<require>` items. Editing a site package's `package.xml` in its source repository is still
> the clearest way to change it.

- The root `version` becomes `3.5.2`; attributes the kernel does not know are dropped.
- `<files>` is left out when there is no file.
- `<settings>` is left out when the package has no settings file.
- A dependency item is written with `type`, `name`, `value` (when not empty) and, from 6.0.15 on, every other
  attribute it was read with (`min-version`, `max-version` ...). Before 6.0.15 those were dropped, so a stored site
  package lost its version requirements.
